2q37 monosomy is a rare [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) caused by a [deletion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deletion_(genetics)) of a segment at the end of [chromosome 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_2).

three-base periodicity property in the field of [Genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) is a property that is characteristic of protein-coding [DNA sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence).

3-Hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA deacylase deficiency is a rare [autosomal recessive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominance_(genetics)) condition that is associated with severely delayed psychomotor development, [neurodegeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurodegeneration), increased [lactic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lactic_acid) and brain lesions in the [basal ganglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basal_ganglia).
3-M syndrome or 3M3 is a rare hereditary disorder characterized by severe growth retardation, [facial dysmorphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_dysmorphism), and skeletal abnormalities.

454 Life Sciences was a biotechnology company based in [Branford, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branford,_Connecticut) that specialized in high-throughput [DNA sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing).

5-base sequencing refers to the detection of five [nucleotide bases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide_base) in DNA, including the four standard bases ([adenine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adenine), [guanine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guanine), [cytosine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytosine), and [thymine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thymine)) and a modified base, [5-methylcytosine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5-Methylcytosine) (5mC), an important [epigenetic marker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenetic_marker).

8p23.1 duplication syndrome is a rare [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) caused by a [duplication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_duplication) of a region from human [chromosome 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_8).

9-Aminoacridine is a synthetic dye used clinically as a topical [antiseptic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiseptic) and experimentally as a [mutagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutagen), an [intracellular pH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracellular_pH) indicator and a small molecule [MALDI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MALDI) matrix.
Aortic aneurysm, familial abdominal 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the AAA1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

definition: allele frequency spectrum, sometimes called the site frequency spectrum, is the [distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency_distribution) of the [allele frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele_frequency) of a given set of [loci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)) (often [SNPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNPs)) in a population or sample.
anti-sense oligonucleotide (ASO) is a short piece of synthetic [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) complementary to the sequence of a variable target DNA.
Allelic exclusion is a process by which only one [allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele) of a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) is expressed while the other allele is silenced.

Allograft inflammatory factor 1-like is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that is encoded by the AIF1L [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) in [humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human).

Allotopic expression (AE) refers to expression of [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes) in the [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) that normally are expressed only from the [mitochondrial genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrial_genome).
Allregulin (ARLN) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) which in humans is encoded by the C4orf3 gene.

Alternating hemiplegia (also known as crossed hemiplegia) is a form of [hemiplegia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemiplegia) that has an ipsilateral cranial nerve palsies and contralateral hemiplegia or hemiparesis of extremities of the body.

Alwadei syndrome or autosomal recessive mental retardation-61 (MRT61) is an [autosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosome) [recessive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominance_(genetics)) [neurodevelopmental disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurodevelopmental_disorder) characterized by [delayed psychomotor development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychomotor_learning), [intellectual disability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_disability), and variable abnormal [facial features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face).

definition: Ambidirectional dominance occurs in a situation where multiple [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s influence a [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) and [dominance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominance_(genetics)) is in different directions depending on the gene.

ambush hypothesis is a hypothesis in the field of [molecular genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_genetics) that suggests that the prevalence of “hidden” or [off-frame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frameshift_mutation) [stop codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_codon)s in [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) selectively deters off-frame [translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)) of [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messenger_RNA) to save energy, molecular resources, and to reduce strain on biosynthetic machinery by truncating the production of non-functional, potentially cytotoxic protein products.

Amelogenins are a group of [protein isoforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_isoforms) produced by [alternative splicing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_splicing) or [proteolysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteolysis) from the [AMELX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMELX) gene, on the [X chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_chromosome), and also the [AMELY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMELY) gene in males, on the [Y chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y_chromosome).

Amelogenin, Y isoform is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the AMELY [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

American Journal of Medical Genetics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) dealing with [human genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genetics) published in three separate sections (parts) by [Wiley-Liss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Liss): * American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A * American Journal of Medical Genetics Part B: Neuropsychiatric Genetics * American Journal of Medical Genetics Part C: Seminars in Medical Genetics Until 1996 they were one journal under the name American Journal of Medical Genetics, when they split into Part A and Part B.
American Society of Human Genetics (ASHG), founded in 1948, is a professional membership organization for specialists in [human genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genetics).

definition: Ames test is a widely employed method that uses [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) to test whether a given chemical can cause [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation)s in the [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) of the test organism.
Autocrine motility factor receptor, isoform 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the AMFR [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
amnesiac (amn) gene in [Drosophila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drosophila_melanogaster) is a mutant suppressor of the [dunce gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunce).
AMP deaminase 3 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the AMPD3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

amplicon sequence variant (ASV) is any one of the inferred single [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequences recovered from a high-throughput analysis of [marker gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marker_gene)s.

Amplified fragment length polymorphism (AFLP-PCR or AFLP) is a [PCR-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) tool used in [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) research, [DNA fingerprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_fingerprint)ing, and in the practice of [genetic engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_engineering).

Amplified rDNA (Ribosomal DNA) Restriction Analysis is the extension of the technique of RFLP ([restriction fragment length polymorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restriction_fragment_length_polymorphism)) to the gene encoding the [small (16s) ribosomal subunit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16S_ribosomal_RNA) of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).

Analysis of molecular variance (AMOVA), is a [statistical model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_model) for the molecular algorithm in a single [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species), typically [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology).

CFAP97D2 (Cilia and Flagella Associated Protein 97 Domain containing 2) is a protein that in humans is encoded by the CFAP97D2 gene.

CG suppression is a term for the phenomenon that [CG dinucleotides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CpG_site) are very uncommon in most portions of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) genomes.

cGAS–STING pathway (cyclic GMP-AMP synthase - stimulator of interferon genes) is a component of the [innate immune system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Innate_immune_system) that functions to detect the presence of [cytosol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytosol)ic [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and, in response, trigger expression of inflammatory genes that can lead to [senescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senescence) Furthermore, the enhanced stability of cGAMP, due to the unique 2'-5' phosphodiester bond, may make it a preferred adjuvant to DNA for in vivo applications.

Chromatin assembly factor 1 subunit B is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the CHAF1B [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Chakragati mouse (ckr) is an insertional [transgenic mouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgenic_mouse) [mutant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutant) ([Mus musculus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_mouse)) displaying [hyperactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperactivity) behaviour and circling.

Chromosome alignment-maintaining phosphoprotein 1 (CHAMP1) also known as zinc finger protein 828 (ZNF828) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the CHAMP1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Chem-seq is a technique that is used to map [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome)-wide interactions between small [molecules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecules) and their [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) targets in the [chromatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatin) of [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) [cell nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nuclei).

Chemical genetics is the investigation of the function of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s and [signal transduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_transduction) pathways in cells by the [screening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-throughput_screening) of [chemical libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_library) of [small molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_molecule)s.
Chemically induced dimerization (CID) is a biological mechanism in which two proteins bind only in the presence of a certain small molecule, enzyme or other dimerizing agent.
Chemogenetics is the process by which [macromolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macromolecule)s can be engineered to interact with previously unrecognized small molecules.

Chemogenomics, or chemical genomics, is the systematic [screening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-throughput_screening) of targeted [chemical libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_library) of [small molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_molecule)s against individual [drug target](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_target) families (e.g., [GPCRs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G_protein-coupled_receptor), [nuclear receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_receptor)s, [kinase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinase)s, [protease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protease)s, etc.) with the ultimate goal of identification of novel [drug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug)s and drug targets.

Chi site or Chi sequence is a short stretch of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) in the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) of a [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium) near which [homologous recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologous_recombination) is more likely to occur than on average across the genome.

chiasma (: chiasmata) is the point of contact, the physical link, between two (non-sister) [chromatid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatid)s belonging to [homologous chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologous_chromosome)s.

ChIL sequencing (ChIL-seq), also known as Chromatin Integration Labeling sequencing, is a method used to analyze [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) interactions with [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

Chillingham cattle, also known as Chillingham wild cattle, is a breed of [cattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cattle) that live in a large enclosed park at [Chillingham Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chillingham_Castle), [Northumberland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northumberland), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England).
CHIME syndrome, also known as Zunich–Kaye syndrome or Zunich neuroectodermal syndrome, is a rare [congenital ichthyosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congenital_ichthyosis) first described in 1983.

definition: genetic chimerism or chimera ([en-US](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/En-US)), also chimaerism or chimaera ([en-UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/En-UK)), ( ) is a single [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) composed of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) of different [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype)s.
chimera is a single DNA sequence originating when multiple [transcripts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(biology)) or DNA sequences get joined.
Chimeraplasty is a non-viral method of [gene therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_therapy).

Chimeric nucleases are an example of [engineered proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_engineering) which must comprise a [DNA-binding domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA-binding_domain) to give sequence specificity and a [nuclease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclease) domain for [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) cleavage.

Chimpanzee stool associated circular virus is a single stranded [DNA virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_virus) isolated from [chimpanzee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_chimpanzee) [stool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feces).
China National GeneBank or CNGB () is China's first national-level [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) storage bank, approved and funded by the Chinese government.

ChIP-exo is a [chromatin immunoprecipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatin_immunoprecipitation) based method for mapping the locations at which a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) of interest ([transcription factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_factor)) binds to the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

ChIP-on-chip (also known as ChIP-chip) is a technology that combines [chromatin immunoprecipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatin_immunoprecipitation) ('ChIP') with [DNA microarray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_microarray) ( ==Further reading== * * == External links == * http://www.genome.gov/10005107 ENCODE project * [https://amkor.com/technology/chip-on-chip/ Chip-on-Chip (CoC)] Package Information from [Amkor Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amkor_Technology) ===Analysis and software=== *[http://www.ciml.univ-mrs.fr/software/cocas/index.html] CoCAS: a free Analysis software for Agilent ChIP-on-Chip experiments *[http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/2.4/bioc/html/rMAT.html] rMAT: R implementation from MAT program to normalize and analyze tiling arrays and ChIP-chip data.

ChiRP-Seq (Chromatin Isolation by [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) purification) is a [high-throughput sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-throughput_sequencing) method to discover regions of the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) which are bound by a specific RNA (or by a ribonucleoprotein containing the RNA of interest).

chlorophycean mitochondrial code (translation table 16) is a [genetic code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) found in the [mitochondria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondria) of [Chlorophyceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorophyceae).

chloroplast capture is a process through which inter-species [hybridization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_(biology)) and subsequent [backcrosses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backcrossing) yield a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) with a new combination of [nuclear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_DNA) and [chloroplast genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroplast_genome)s.

Chlorovirus, also known as Chlorella virus, is a genus of giant double-stranded [DNA virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_virus)es, in the family [Phycodnaviridae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phycodnaviridae).
Charged multivesicular body protein 5 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the CHMP5 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Chondrolectin is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the CHODL [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Chondrodysplasia Grebe type is a rare [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder).

Chordate genomics is the study of the evolution of the [chordate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chordate) [clade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clade) based on a comparison of the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome)s of several [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) within the clade.

choriogenesis is the formation of the [chorion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chorion), an outer membrane of the placenta that eventually forms [chorionic villi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chorionic_villi) that allow the transfer of blood and nutrients from mother to fetus.

Choroideremia (; CHM) is a rare, [X-linked recessive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-linked_recessive) form of hereditary [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina)l degeneration that affects roughly 1 in 50,000 males.

chromosomal rearrangement is a [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) that is a type of [chromosome abnormality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_abnormality) involving a change in the structure of the native [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome).

definition: 6-deoxyerythronolide B hydroxylase is an [Actinomycetota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actinomycetota) [Cytochrome P450](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytochrome_P450) [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) originally from [Saccharopolyspora erythraea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saccharopolyspora_erythraea), catalyzes the 6S-hydroxylate of [6-deoxyerythronolide B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6-deoxyerythronolide_B) (6-DEB) to [erythronolide B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erythronolide_B) (EB) which is the first step of biosynthesis of the [macrolide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macrolide) antibiotic [erythromycin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erythromycin).
Cytodeme is the total assembly of organisms that use an identical suite of chromosomes to carry their genes.

Cytogenetic and Genome Research is the name of a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that was established in 1962.

cytohet (or heteroplasmon) is a [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) whose [non-nuclear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) is [heterozygous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterozygous).

Cytonuclear discordance, also known as mitonuclear discordance, mito-nuclear discordance, or nuclear-mitochondrial discordance, describes the discrepancy in [phylogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylogenetics) relationships using [mitochondrial DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrial_DNA) (mtDNA) versus nuclear genes (or [nuclear DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_DNA), nDNA).
Cytotaxonomy is the classification of organisms using comparative studies of [chromosomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) during [meosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meosis).

Cysteine and tyrosine-rich protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the CYYR1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) alternative splicing and expression of the CYYR1 (cysteine/tyrosine-rich 1) mRNA in human neuroendocrine tumors |journal=BMC Cancer |volume=7|article-number= 66 |year= 2007 |pmid= 17442112 |doi= 10.1186/1471-2407-7-66 | pmc=1863428 |name-list-style=vanc| author2=Frabetti F | author3=Hunt
CZIB is a gene in the [human genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genome) that encodes the protein CXXC motif containing zinc binding protein.
D-amino acid oxidase activator (DAOA, also known as G72) is a protein enriched in various parts of brain, spinal cord, and testis.

displacement loop or D-loop is a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) structure where the two strands of a double-stranded DNA molecule are separated for a stretch and held apart by a third strand of DNA.

D-loop replication is a proposed process by which [circular DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_DNA_(disambiguation)) molecules like those found in many (though not all) [chloroplast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroplast)s and [mitochondria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondria) replicate their genetic material.
Disabled homolog 2-interacting protein is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DAB2IP [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

dachshund (dac) is a gene involved in the development of the [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod) [compound eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compound_eye) Its homologs form the SKI/SNO/DAC family ().

DAF-14 is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) of the [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode) [Caenorhabditis elegans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caenorhabditis_elegans) encoding a [R-SMAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R-SMAD) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) of [TGF-beta signaling pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TGF-beta_signaling_pathway), which will be [phosphorylated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphorylates) and forms a [heterodimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterodimer) with phosphorylated [daf-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daf-8) when the TGF-β ligand [daf-7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daf-7) binds to the TGF-β receptors [daf-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daf-1)/[daf-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daf-4), then the heterodimer enter to the [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) to inhibit transcription regulated by [daf-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daf-3)/[daf-5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daf-5).

DAF-3 or Dwarfin sma is a [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode) [Caenorhabditis elegans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caenorhabditis_elegans) [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) encoding a Co-SMAD [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) of [TGF-beta signaling pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TGF-beta_signaling_pathway).

Daf-5 is an [ortholog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ortholog) of the mammalian [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) [Sno/Ski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SKI_protein)，which present in the nematode worm [Caenorhabditis elegans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caenorhabditis_elegans) on the downstream of [TGFβ signaling pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TGFβ_signaling_pathway).

DAF-8 [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode) [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) encoding a [R-SMAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R-SMAD) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) of [TGF-beta signaling pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TGF-beta_signaling_pathway), which was originally found in [model organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_organism) [Caenorhabditis elegans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caenorhabditis_elegans).

Dally (division abnormally delayed) is the name of a gene that encodes a HS-modified-protein found in the fruit fly [Drosophila melanogaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drosophila_melanogaster).

DAPI (pronounced 'DAPPY', /ˈdæpiː/), or 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole, is a [fluorescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluorescence) [stain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staining_(biology)) that binds strongly to [adenine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adenine)–[thymine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thymine)-rich regions in [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).
Death-associated protein kinase 1 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the DAPK1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

dark taxon ( dark taxa) is a term generally to denote [taxa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxon) belonging to groups for which the number of estimated [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) greatly surpasses the number of species currently [described](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species_description).

Darlington Lecture is a lectureship of the [John Innes Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Innes_Centre) named after its former director, the [geneticist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneticist) [[C.
Aspartyl-tRNA Synthetase 2, Mitochondrial is an enzyme which is encoded by the gene DARS2.

Darwinian threshold or Darwinian transition is a term introduced by [Carl Woese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Woese) to describe a transition period during the [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) of the first [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) when [genetic transmission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_(genetics)) moves from a predominantly horizontal mode to a vertical mode.

definition: David Dexter Perkins (May 2, 1919 – January 2, 2007) was an American [geneticist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneticist), a member of the faculty of the Department of Biology at [Stanford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University) for more than 58 years, from 1948 until his death in 2007.

David Reich Lab is a research laboratory located within the Department of Genetics at [Harvard Medical School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Medical_School) in [Boston, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston,_Massachusetts).

DAVID syndrome, short for deficient anterior pituitary with variable immune deficiency syndrome, is a rare [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) that is characterized by [adrenocorticotropic hormone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrenocorticotropic_hormone) deficiency combined with [common variable immunodeficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_variable_immunodeficiency) and [hypogammaglobulinemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypogammaglobulinemia), which is caused by a [heterozygous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygosity) mutation in the [NFKB2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFKB2) gene.
DAZ-associated protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DAZAP1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Deleted in bladder cancer protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DBC1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Sister chromatid cohesion protein DCC1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DSCC1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
dcGO is a comprehensive ontology database for protein domains.

DCL2 (an abbreviation of Dicer-like 2) is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) in plants that codes for the DCL2 [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein), a [ribonuclease III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribonuclease_III) [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) involved in processing exogenous [double-stranded RNA (dsRNA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-stranded_RNA) into 22 nucleotide [small interference RNAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_interfering_RNA) (siRNAs).
DCL4 (Dicer-like 4) is a plant gene that encodes an enzyme involved in RNA silencing, a process by which cells regulate gene expression and defend against viruses.

DICER-LIKE 5 (DCL5) is a plant [Dicer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicer)-like endoribonuclease that functions in the biogenesis of 24-nucleotide reproductive phased small interfering RNAs ([phasiRNAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PhasiRNAs)).
Dynactin subunit 3 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DCTN3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Dynactin 5 (p25) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DCTN5 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
DEAD (Asp-Glu-Ala-Asp) box polypeptide 27, also known as DDX27, is a human [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
DEAD (Asp-Glu-Ala-Asp) box polypeptide 31, also known as DDX31, is a human [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
DDX3X syndrome is a genetic disorder that affects predominantly females.
de Finetti diagram is a [ternary plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ternary_plot) used in [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics).

De novo [domestication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestication) is a process where new [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) are genetically altered to meet [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) needs, such as [agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture) or [companionship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet).
de novo mutation is a newly present [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) in an individual organism.

De novo sequence assemblers are a type of program that assembles short [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide) sequences into longer ones without the use of a reference [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

DEAD RNA motif is a conserved [non-coding RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-coding_RNA) (ncRNA) found in the introns of [DEAD-box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DEAD_box) RNA helicase genes across land plants.
Deleted in esophageal cancer 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DEC1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
DECIPHER is a web-based resource and database of genomic variation data from analysis of patient [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

definition: decipherment is the discovery of the meaning of the symbols found in extinct [language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language)s and/or [alphabet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphabet)s.

deCODE genetics () is a [biopharmaceutical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopharmaceutical) company based in [Reykjavík](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reykjavík), [Iceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceland).

definition: Decreased DNA Methylation I (DDM1), is a plant gene that encodes a nucleosome remodeler which facilitates [DNA methylation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_methylation).

Dedicator of cytokinesis protein 11 (Dock11), also known as Zizimin2, is a large (~240 kDa) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) encoded in the human by the DOCK11 gene, involved in [intracellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracellular) [signalling networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_signalling).

Dedicator of cytokinesis protein 9 (Dock9), also known as Zizimin1, is a large (~230 kDa) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) encoded in the human by the DOCK9 gene, involved in [intracellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracellular) [signalling networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_signalling).
DEFICIENS is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) that regulates [floral architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floral_architecture).
[schema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schema_(genetic_algorithms)) (plural: schemata) is a template that represents a subset of potential solutions.

DeFries–Fulker (DF) regression, also sometimes called DeFries–Fulker extremes analysis, is a type of [multiple regression analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_regression_analysis) designed for estimating the magnitude of genetic and environmental effects in [twin studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin_studies).

Degenerative suspensory ligament desmitis, commonly called DSLD, also known as equine systemic proteoglycan accumulation (ESPA), is a systemic disease of the [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) of the [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) and other [equines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equus_(genus)).
Delta(4)-desaturase, sphingolipid 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DEGS2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Chromosome 16p12.2-p11.2 deletion syndrome is a gene deletion syndrome in the position 16p12.2-p11.2 of the human genome.
Chromosome 17p13.1 deletion syndrome is a [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) in humans that is designed DEL17P13.1.

deletion (also called gene deletion, deficiency, or [deletion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deletion_anomaly) mutation) (sign: [Δ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_(letter))) is a [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) (a genetic aberration) in which a part of a [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) or a sequence of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) is left out during DNA replication.
deletion mapping is a technique used to find out the [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) sites within a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Delitto perfetto () is a genetic technique for in vivo [site-directed mutagenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site-directed_mutagenesis) in yeast.
deme, in the strict sense, is a group of individuals that belong to the same [taxonomic group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomic_group).

Demethylating agents are chemical substances that can inhibit [methylation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methylation), resulting in the expression of the previously hypermethylated silenced [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes) (see [[Methylation#Cancer]] for more detail).
demethylation inhibitor is a compound that blocks the removal of [methyl group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methyl_group)s.

Modern application of denaturation mapping: DNA is stained with a dye(green) that dissociates from single stranded DNA, changes in the environment like temperature increases that are not enough to completely dissociate the molecule causes parts of it to dissociate in a predictable manner from AT rich regions (red).

Denis Oswald Jordan (23 September 1914, [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London) – 12 February 1982, [St Georges, South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Georges,_South_Australia)) was an Anglo-Australian chemist with a distinguished career as a researcher and lecturer in Chemistry at both [University College Nottingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College_Nottingham) (1940–53) and the [University of Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Adelaide), where he was [Angas Professor of Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angas_Professor_of_Chemistry) from 1958 to 1982.
DENN domain-containing protein 1A is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DENND1A [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
C-myc promoter-binding protein is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DENND4A [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Denny (Denisova 11) is an ~90,000 year old fossil specimen belonging to a ~13-year-old [Neanderthal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neanderthal)-[Denisovan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denisovan) hybrid girl.
related: Interbreeding between archaic and modern humans

definition: Dentinogenesis imperfecta (DI) is a [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) of [tooth development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_tooth_development).

Deoxyribozymes, also called DNA enzymes, DNAzymes, or catalytic DNA, are [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) [oligonucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligonucleotide)s that are capable of performing a specific [chemical reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction), often but not always [catalytic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalysis).

page: Department of Genetics, University of Cambridge

definition: DEP domain containing 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) in humans that is encoded by the DEPDC1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
DEP Domain Containing Protein 7 (DEPDC7) is a protein of unknown function located on [chromosome 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_11) bases 33,015,863-33,033,581.

Dermatoglyphics () is the scientific study of [fingerprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fingerprint)s, lines, mounts and shapes of hands, as distinct from the superficially similar [pseudoscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudoscience) of [palmistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmistry).

DeSanto–Shinawi (DESSH) syndrome is a rare genetic disorder caused by genetic variations (mutations) in a gene called [WW Domain-Containing Adaptor with Coiled-coil Region (WAC gene)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WAC_(gene)).

designer baby is an [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo) or [fetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetus) whose [genetic makeup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) has been intentionally selected or altered, often to exclude a particular [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) or to remove genes associated with disease, to achieve desired traits.

Desmin-related myofibrillar myopathy, is a subgroup of the [myofibrillar myopathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myofibrillar_myopathy) diseases and is the result of a mutation in the gene that codes for [desmin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desmin) which prevents it from forming [protein filament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_filament)s, instead forming aggregates of desmin and other proteins throughout the cell.
Desmoglein-3 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DSG3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Desmoglein-4 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DSG4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

term: Deterministic Barcoding in Tissue for Spatial Omics Sequencing
page: Deterministic Barcoding in Tissue for Spatial Omics Sequencing
definition: Deterministic Barcoding in Tissue for Spatial Omics Sequencing (DBiT-seq) was developed at [Yale University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University) by Rong Fan and colleagues in 2020 to create a [multi-omics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-omics) approach for studying spatial [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) heterogenicity within a tissue sample.
Developmental homeostasis is a process in which animals and plants develop more or less normally, despite defective [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes) and deficient environments.

Developmental noise or [stochastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic) noise is a concept within [developmental biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology) in which the observable characteristics or traits ([phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype)) varies between individuals even though both individuals share the same [genetic code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) ([genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype)s) and the other [environmental factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_factor)s are completely the same.
Whirlin is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DFNB31 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Dehydrogenase/reductase SDR family member 1, also known as Short chain dehydrogenase/reductase family 19C member 1 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the DHRS1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) located on [chromosome 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_14).

Putative pre-mRNA-splicing factor ATP-dependent RNA helicase DHX15 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the DHX15 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Diablo homolog (DIABLO) is a [mitochondrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrial) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DIABLO (direct [IAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inhibitor_of_apoptosis) binding protein with low pI) [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) on chromosome 12.

diallel cross is a mating scheme used by [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_breeding) and [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_breeding) breeders, as well as [geneticists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantitative_genetics), to investigate the genetic underpinnings of quantitative traits.

definition: Differential extraction (also known as differential lysis) refers to the process by which the DNA from two different types of cells can be extracted without mixing their contents.
Diffuse panbronchiolitis (DPB) is an [inflammatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation) [lung disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung_disease) of unknown cause.
categories: Genetic disorders with OMIM but no gene

definition: Digital sequence information (DSI) is a placeholder term used in international policy fora, particularly the [Convention on Biological Diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_on_Biological_Diversity) (CBD), to refer to data derived from dematerialized [genetic resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_resources) (GR).

Dilated cardiomyopathy with ataxia syndrome is a multi-systemic [hereditary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hereditary) disorder that is characterized by heart abnormalities and problems with coordination, movement and balance.
Dingo–dog hybrid is a cross between a [dingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dingo) and a [domestic dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_dog).

Dinoflagellate/viral nucleoproteins (DVNPs) are a family of positively-charged, [DNA-binding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA-binding_protein) [nucleoproteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleoproteins) found exclusively in [dinoflagellates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinoflagellates) and [Nucleocytoviricota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleocytoviricota).
Disco-interacting protein 2 homolog A is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DIP2A [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
DIP2 disco-interacting protein 2 homolog B (Drosophila) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DIP2B [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Divergent protein kinase domain 1C is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DIPK1C [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Diploidization is the process of converting a polyploid genome back into a diploid one.

DiProDB is a [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_structure_database) designed to collect and analyse [thermodynamic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamics), [structural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_structure) and other [dinucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinucleotide) properties.

GTP-binding protein Di-Ras3 (DIRAS3) also known as aplysia ras homology member I (ARHI) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DIRAS3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Direct repeats are a type of genetic sequence that consists of two or more repeats of a specific sequence.

Directionality, in [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) and [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), is the end-to-end chemical orientation of a single strand of [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid).
Exosome complex exonuclease RRP44 or Dis3 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the DIS3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Disassortative mating (also known as negative assortative mating or heterogamy) is a mating pattern in which individuals with dissimilar [phenotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypes) mate with one another more frequently than would be expected under [random mating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_mating).
Dische test, or Dische reaction, is used to distinguish [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) from [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA).

Disease gene identification is a process by which scientists identify the mutant [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype)s responsible for an inherited [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder).

definition: DISGENET is an AI-ready translational knowledge infrastructure that integrates comprehensive information on human genotype–phenotype relationships, including gene–disease, variant–disease, and disease–disease associations.

page: Dishevelled binding antagonist of beta catenin 1
definition: Dishevelled binding antagonist of beta catenin 1 (Dact1, previously known as Dapper, Dpr1, Frodo) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DACT1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

term: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy type V
page: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy type V
definition: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy type V is a particular type of neuropathic disorder.

Distal promoter elements are [regulatory DNA sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulatory_sequence) that can be many kilobases distant from the [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) that they regulate.

Distal spinal muscular atrophy type 2 (DSMA2), also known as Jerash type distal hereditary motor neuropathy (HMNJ), is a very rare childhood-onset genetic disorder characterised by progressive muscle wasting affecting lower and subsequently upper limbs.

definition: Distyly is a breeding system in plants that is characterized by two separate flower morphs, where individual plants produce flowers that have either long styles and short stamens (L-morph flowers) or short styles and long stamens (S-morph flowers).

Diversity Arrays Technology (DArT) is a high-throughput genetic marker technique that can detect allelic variations to provide comprehensive [genome coverage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coverage_(genetics)) without any DNA sequence information for [genotyping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotyping) and other genetic analysis.

diversity panel is a collection of genetic material or individual samples taken from a diverse [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) of a certain [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).

Diversity-generating retroelements (DGRs) are a family of [retroelements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retroelements) that were first found in [Bordetella phage (BPP-1)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordetella_virus_BPP1), [[Category:Mobile genetic elements]] [[Category:Molecular biology]] 2o3zpwra0x6cjmhjc3urzt9rn9w7zx3
Dixin is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DIXDC1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

DLD/NP1 is a [tumor suppressor gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor_suppressor_gene) discovered by a team of medical students from an [American University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_University) in [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon).

PSD-95 (postsynaptic density protein 95) also known as SAP-90 (synapse-associated protein 90) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DLG4 (discs large homolog 4) [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Disks large-associated protein 1 (DAP-1), also known as guanylate kinase-associated protein (GKAP), is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the DLGAP1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Transmembrane protein 261 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the TMEM261 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) located on [chromosome 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_9).

DNA adduct, at center]] In [molecular genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_genetics), a DNA adduct is a segment of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) bound to a [cancer-causing chemical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcinogen).

definition: DNA analyzer is a device used to determine characteristics of a person's [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).

definition: DNA barcoding is a method of species identification using a short section of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) from a specific [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) or genes.

DNA barcoding in diet assessment is the use of [DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_barcoding) to analyse the [diet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diet_(nutrition)) of organisms === Birds === === Fish === === Arthropods === == See also == * [Fish DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_DNA_barcoding) * Aquatic macroinvertebrates DNA barcoding * [Microbial DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_DNA_barcoding) * [Algae DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae_DNA_barcoding) * [Pollen DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen_DNA_barcoding) == References == [[Category:Bioinformatics]] [[Category:DNA

DNA base flipping, or nucleotide flipping, is a mechanism in which a single [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide) base, or [nucleobase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleobase), is rotated outside the nucleic acid double helix.
DNA binding sites are a type of [binding site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binding_site) found in [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) where other molecules may bind.

DNA computing is an emerging branch of [unconventional computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unconventional_computing) which uses [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), and [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology) hardware, instead of the traditional [electronic computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_computing).

DNA condensation refers to the process of compacting [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) molecules [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro) or [in vivo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vivo).

DNA construct is an artificially-designed segment of DNA borne on a [vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_(molecular_biology)) that can be used to incorporate genetic material into a target [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_tissue) or [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

DNA curtain is a [single-molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-molecule_experiment) imaging technique used to visualize [protein–DNA interactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein-DNA_interaction) in real time with high-throughput.

Natural DNA damage is an alteration in the chemical structure of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), such as a break in a strand of DNA, a [nucleobase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleobase) missing from the backbone of DNA, or a chemically changed base such as [8-OHdG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8-Oxo-2'-deoxyguanosine).

DNA damage theory of aging proposes that [aging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aging) is a consequence of unrepaired accumulation of [naturally occurring DNA damage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_damage_(naturally_occurring)).

DNA database or DNA databank is a [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database) of [DNA profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_profiling)s which can be used in the analysis of [genetic disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disease)s, [genetic fingerprinting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_fingerprinting) for [criminology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminology), or [genetic genealogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_genealogy).

DNA encryption is the process of hiding or perplexing genetic information by a [computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computation)al method in order to improve [genetic privacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_privacy) in [DNA sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) processes.
DNA fragmentation is the separation or breaking of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) strands into pieces.

DNA glycosylases are a family of [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme)s involved in [base excision repair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base_excision_repair), classified under [EC number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme_Commission_number) EC 3.2.2.

DNA ligase is a type of enzyme that facilitates the joining of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) strands together by catalyzing the formation of a [phosphodiester bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphodiester_bond).
DNA ligase 4 or DNA ligase IV is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the LIG4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
DNA machine is a [molecular machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_machine) constructed from [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).
DNA marking is a type of [forensic identification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forensic_identification).

Epigenome editing or epigenome engineering is a type of genetic engineering in which the [epigenome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenome) is modified at specific sites using engineered molecules targeted to those sites (as opposed to whole-genome modifications).

Epigenomics is the study of the complete set of [epigenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenetic) modifications on the genetic material of a cell, known as the [epigenome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenome).

Epistasis and functional genomics is the study of how [genetic interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_interaction)s, where one gene affects the expression of another gene, can be systematically analyzed to elucidate gene function and understand complex genetic pathways.

floxing refers to the [insertion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insertional_mutagenesis) of a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequence (which is then said to be floxed) between two [LoxP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cre-Lox_recombination) sequences, creating an artificial [gene cassette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_cassette) which can then be conditionally [deleted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deletion_(genetics)) (knocked out), [translocated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal_translocation), or [inverted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal_inversion) in a process called [Cre-Lox recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cre-Lox_recombination).

Flp-FRT recombination is a [site-directed recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site-specific_recombination) technology, increasingly used to manipulate an organism's DNA under controlled conditions in vivo.

Gene duplication (or chromosomal duplication or gene amplification) is a mechanism through which new genetic material is generated during [molecular evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_evolution).

gene expression profiling is the measurement of the activity (the [expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression)) of thousands of genes at once, to create a global picture of cellular function.

Gene expression programming (GEP) in [computer programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming) is an [evolutionary algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_algorithm) that creates computer programs or models.
gene family is a set of several similar genes, formed by duplication of a single original [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene), and generally with similar biochemical functions.

gene flow (also known as migration and allele flow) is the transfer of [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation) material from one [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) to another.

gene gun or biolistic particle delivery system is a device used to deliver exogenous [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) ([transgene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgene)s), [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA), or [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) to cells.

gene knock-in (abbreviation: KI) refers to a [genetic engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_engineering) method that involves the one-for-one substitution of DNA sequence information in a [genetic locus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)) or the [insertion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insertion_(genetics)) of sequence information not found within the locus.

Gene knockdown is an experimental technique by which the [expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) of one or more of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)'s [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s is reduced.

Gene nomenclature is the scientific [naming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomenclature) of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s, the units of [heredity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity) in living organisms.
Gene order is the permutation of [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) arrangement.

gene pool is the set of all [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s, or [genetic information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_information), in any [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)), usually of a particular [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).
Gene or genetic redundancy is a term used to describe the existence of multiple [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s in the genome of an organism that perform the same biochemical function.

Genetic regulatory circuits (also referred to as transcriptional regulatory circuits) is a concept that evolved from the [Operon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operon) Model discovered by [François Jacob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/François_Jacob) and [Jacques Monod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Monod).

Gene silencing is the [regulation of gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulation_of_gene_expression) in a cell to prevent the expression of a certain [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Gene targeting is a [biotechnological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology) tool used to change the [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) of an organism (hence it is a form of [genome editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome_editing)).

gene theft or DNA theft is the act of acquiring the [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_material) of another individual, usually from [public places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_space), without their permission.

Gene therapy is [medical technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_technology) that aims to produce a [therapeutic effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Therapeutic_effect) through the manipulation of [gene expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression) or through altering the biological properties of living cells.

definition: A) with typical GTA (gene transfer agent) production and transduction (B).|alt=|330x330px]] Gene transfer agents (GTAs) are DNA-containing [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus)-like particles that are produced by some [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) and [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea) and mediate [horizontal gene transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horizontal_gene_transfer).

Gene trapping is a [high-throughput](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-throughput_screening) approach that is used to introduce insertional [mutations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutations) across an organism's genome.
Gene Wiki is a project within [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia) that aims to describe the relationships and functions of all human [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s.

Gene-environment interplay describes how [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s and [environments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysical_environment) work together to produce a [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype), or observable trait.

genealogical DNA test is a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)-based [genetic test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_testing) used in [genetic genealogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_genealogy) that looks at specific locations of a person's [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) in order to find or verify ancestral [genealogical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogical) relationships, or (with lower reliability) to estimate the [ethnic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnicity) mixture of an individual.

Genecology is a branch of [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology) which studies [genetic variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation) of [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) and [communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community) compared to their [population distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_distribution) in a particular [environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environment_(biophysical)).

GeneNetwork is a combined database and [open-source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software) [bioinformatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics) data analysis software resource for [systems genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systems_genetics).

general mixed Yule–coalescent model (GMYC), also called the generalized mixed Yule–coalescent model, is a method in [molecular phylogenetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_phylogenetics) and [systematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systematics) for inferring putative [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) boundaries from [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) data.

general selection model (GSM) is a model of [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) that describes how a population's [allele frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele_frequencies) will change when acted upon by [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection).

Genesys is an online, global portal about plant [genetic resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_resources) for food and agriculture.

GeneTalk is a web-based platform, tool, and database for filtering, reduction and prioritization of human [sequence variants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation) from [[Next_generation_sequencing#Next-generation_methods|next-generation sequencing]] (NGS) data.
Genetic ablation occurs when a gene is deemed “null” through the homologous [genetic recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_recombination) of a gene.
genetic algebra is a (possibly [non-associative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-associative_algebra)) algebra used to model inheritance in genetics.

definition: Genetic architecture is the underlying genetic basis of a [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) [trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trait_(biological)) and its variational properties.

Genetic association is when one or more [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype)s within a population co-occur with a [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) trait [more often than would be expected by chance occurrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_(statistics)).

Genetic code is a set of rules used by living [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) to [translate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(biology)) information encoded within genetic material ([DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) sequences of nucleotide triplets or [codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codon)s) into [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s.

Genetic counseling is the process of investigating individuals and families affected by or at risk of genetic disorders to help them understand and adapt to the medical, psychological and familial implications of genetic contributions to disease.

genetic demixing refers to a phenomenon in which an initial mixture of individuals with two or more distinct [genotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotypes) rearranges in the course of time, giving birth to a spatial organization where some or all genotypes are concentrated in distinct patches.

definition: Genetic divergence is the process in which two or more populations of an ancestral species accumulate independent genetic changes ([mutations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutations)) through time, often leading to reproductive isolation and continued mutation even after the populations have become [reproductively isolated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_isolation) for some period of time, as there is not any genetic exchange anymore.
Genetic diversity is the total number of [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) characteristics in the genetic makeup of a species.
Genetic ecology is the study of the stability and expression of varying genetic material within abiotic mediums.

Genetic epidemiology is the study of the role of [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) factors in determining health and disease in families and in populations, and the interplay of such genetic factors with environmental factors.

Genetic equilibrium is the condition of an [allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele) or [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype) in a gene pool (such as a population) where the frequency does not change from generation to generation.

Genetic exceptionalism is the belief that [genetic information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_information) is special and so must be treated differently from other types of medical data or other [personally identifiable information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_data).

Genetic fuzzy systems are [fuzzy system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuzzy_system)s constructed by using [genetic algorithms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_algorithms) or genetic programming, which mimic the process of natural evolution, to identify its structure and parameter.

Genetic genealogy is the use of [genealogical DNA test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogical_DNA_test)s, i.e., [DNA profiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_profiling) and [DNA testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_testing), in combination with traditional [genealogical methods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogy), to infer [genetic relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_distance)s between individuals.

Genetic heterogeneity refers to different genetic causes for the same disease and can be classified into three types: allelic heterogeneity, [locus heterogeneity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_heterogeneity), and phenotypic heterogeneity.

definition: [Genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) imbalance is to describe situation when the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) of a cell or organism has more copies of some genes than other genes due to [chromosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomal) [rearrangements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rearrangement_reaction) or [aneuploidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aneuploidy).
Genetic incompatibility describes the process by which mating yields offspring that are nonviable, prone to disease, or genetically defective in some way.
Genetic Information Research Institute (GIRI) is a non-profit institution that was founded in 1994 by [Jerzy Jurka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Jurka).

Genetic linkage is the tendency of [DNA sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence) that are close together on a [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) to be inherited together during the [meiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiosis) phase of [sexual reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_reproduction).

Genetic load is the difference between the [fitness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_(biology)) of an average [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype) in a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) and the fitness of some reference genotype, which may be either the best present in a population, or may be the theoretically [optimal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxima_and_minima) genotype.

mapping functions are used to model the relationship between [map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_mapping) distances (measured in map units or [centimorgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centimorgan)s) and [recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_recombination) frequencies, particularly as these measurements relate to regions encompassed between [genetic marker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_marker)s.

genetic marker is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) or [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) with a known location on a [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) that can be used to identify individuals or [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).
Genetic matchmaking is the idea of matching couples for romantic relationships based on their biological compatibility.

genetic memory refers to an [artificial neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_neural_network) combination of [genetic algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_algorithm) and the mathematical model of [sparse distributed memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparse_distributed_memory).

Genetic monitoring is the use of [molecular markers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_marker) to (i) identify individuals, species or populations, or (ii) to quantify changes in [population genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetic) metrics (such as [effective population size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effective_population_size), [genetic diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_diversity) and population size) over time.

Genetic predisposition refers to a [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) characteristic which influences the possible [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic) development of an individual organism within a species or population under the influence of [environmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_environment) conditions.

Genetic programming (GP) is an [evolutionary algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_algorithm), an artificial intelligence technique mimicking natural evolution, which operates on a population of programs.
Genetic purging is the increased pressure of natural selection against deleterious [alleles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleles) prompted by [inbreeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inbreeding).

Genetic recombination (also known as genetic reshuffling) is the exchange of [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) between different [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s which leads to production of offspring with combinations of traits that differ from those found in either parent.

Genetic reductionism is the belief that understanding [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s is sufficient to understand all aspects of [human behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_behavior).
Genetic rescue is seen as a mitigation strategy designed to restore genetic diversity and reduce extinction risks in small, isolated and frequently inbred populations.

Genetic resources are genetic material of actual or potential value, where genetic material means any material of plant, animal, [microbial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_genetics) or other origin containing functional units of [heredity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity).

neutral network is a set of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s all related by [point mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_mutation)s that have equivalent function or [fitness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_(biology)).

definition: NF-kappa-B-activating protein is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NKAP [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nuclear factor 1 B-type is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NFIB [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nuclear factor, interleukin 3 regulated, also known as NFIL3 or E4BP4 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) which in humans is encoded by the NFIL3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Nuclear factor 1 X-type is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NFIX [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nuclear factor of kappa light polypeptide gene enhancer in B-cells inhibitor, delta also known as IκBNS is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) in humans that is encoded by the NFKBID [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Transcriptional repressor NF-X1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NFX1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

NgAgo is a [single-stranded DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-stranded_DNA) (ssDNA)-guided [Argonaute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argonaute) [endonuclease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endonuclease), an acronym for [Natronobacterium gregoryi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natronobacterium_gregoryi) Argonaute.
Protein BEX3 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NGFRAP1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

NGLY1 deficiency is a very rare [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) caused by [biallelic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosomal_recessive) pathogenic [variants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) in [NGLY1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NGLY1).

NR4A1 gene is a [transcription factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_factor) important in the development of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s that secrete the [hormone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hormone) [insulin-like 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INSL3) (INSL3).

Niche microdifferentiation is the process a species undergoes to reach [genetic diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_diversity) within that species; it is the process by which an [ecotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecotype) is created.

nick is a discontinuity in a double stranded [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) molecule where there is no [phosphodiester bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphodiester_bond) between adjacent [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide)s of one [[DNA#Overview of molecular structure|strand]].

Nick Craddock is a British [psychiatrist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychiatrist), the director of the National Centre for Mental Health and professor of [psychiatry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychiatry) at [Cardiff University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_University) in Wales.

definition: Nicking Enzyme Amplification Reaction (NEAR) is a method for [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro) [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) amplification like the [polymerase chain reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) (PCR).

NIDDM1 [genetic linkage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_linkage) region refers to a segment on [chromosome 2q](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_2q) that was first identified through genome-wide scans in families with [type 2 diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_2_diabetes), particularly among Mexican American populations.
Nidogen-1 (NID-1), formerly known as entactin, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NID1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nidogen-2, also known as osteonidogen, is a [basal lamina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basal_lamina) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) of the [nidogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nidogen) family.

nif genes are [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s encoding enzymes involved in the [fixation of atmospheric nitrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen_fixation) into a form of [nitrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen) available to living organisms.
nik operon is an [operon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operon) required for uptake of nickel ions into the cell.
[Ninein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninein)-like protein is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NINL [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Ninjurin-1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) encoded by the NINJ1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) in humans.

Non-imprinted in Prader-Willi/Angelman syndrome region protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NIPA1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nipa‐Like Domain‐Containing 4, also known as NIPAL4 or Ichthyin, is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) that is predicted to [code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) for a [transmembrane protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmembrane_protein) with nine [transmembrane domains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmembrane_domains).
