definition: Nix is a [pro-apoptotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-apoptotic) [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) that is regulated by [Histotoxic hypoxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histotoxic_hypoxia).

NK-92 cell line is an [immortalised cell line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immortalised_cell_line) that has the characteristics of a type of [immune cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_blood_cell) found in human blood called '[natural killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_killer_cell)' (NK) cells.
NKAPD1 (NF-kappa-B-activating protein domain containing 1) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein), which in humans, is encoded by the [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) NKAPD1.
Natural killer cell granule protein 7 (NKG7 protein) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NKG7 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
NF-κB inhibitor interacting Ras-like 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NKIRAS2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
NK3 homeobox 3, also known as NKX3-3, zax, bagpipe homeobox or zampogna is a paralogous [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) of [NKX3-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NKX3-2).

NLRP10, short for [NOD-like receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOD-like_receptor) family [pyrin domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrin_domain) containing 10, is an [intracellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracellular) protein of mammals that functions in [apoptosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apoptosis) and the [immune system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_system).
NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NLRP2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 4 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NLRP4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

NLRP6, short for [NOD-like receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOD-like_receptor) family [pyrin domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrin_domain) containing 6, is an [intracellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracellular) protein that plays a role in the [immune system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_system).
NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 7 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NLRP7 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

NLRP8, short for [NOD-like receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOD-like_receptor) family [pyrin domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrin_domain) containing 8, is an [intracellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracellular) protein that is expressed in the [ovaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovary), [testes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testes), and pre[implantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Implantation_(human_embryo)) [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)s of mammals.

NLRP9, short for [NOD-like receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOD-like_receptor) family [pyrin domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrin_domain) containing 9, is an [intracellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracellular) protein that is expressed in the [ovaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovary), [testes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testes), [oocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oocyte)s, and pre[implantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Implantation_(human_embryo)) [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)s of mammals that is likely involved in [reproductive processes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproduction).
Nicotinamide mononucleotide adenylyltransferase 3 (NMNAT3) is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the NMNAT3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Nitric oxide associated 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) in humans that is encoded by the NOA1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nocturnin is a human [hydrolase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrolase) enzyme that is involved in metabolism and its expression is controlled by the rhythmic [circadian clock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circadian_clock).

Non-obese diabetic or NOD [mice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_mouse), like [biobreeding rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biobreeding_rat)s, are used as an [animal model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_organism) for [type 1 diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_1_diabetes).

Noggin, also known as NOG, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that is involved in the development of many [body tissues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)), including [nerve tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_tissue), [muscles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeletal_muscle), and [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s.
Nucleolar protein 4 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NOL4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Nucleolar protein 6 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NOL6 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Nucleolar protein 8 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NOL8 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Nucleolar protein with MIF4G domain 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NOM1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nucleosome Occupancy and Methylome Sequencing (NOMe-seq) is a [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) technique used to simultaneously detect [nucleosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleosome) positioning and [DNA methylation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_methylation).

Non-B DNA is [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) in any conformation other than the canonical ([B-DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-DNA)) conformation, the most common form of DNA found in nature at neutral pH and physiological salt concentrations.

Non-allelic homologous recombination (NAHR) is a form of [homologous recombination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologous_recombination) that occurs between two lengths of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) that have high sequence similarity, but are not [allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele)s.

Non-coding DNA (ncDNA) sequences are components of an organism's [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) that do not [encode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_code) [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) sequences.

non-coding RNA (ncRNA) is a functional [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) molecule that is not [translated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(genetics)) into a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein).
Non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) is a pathway that repairs double-strand breaks in DNA.
Non-Mendelian inheritance is any pattern in which traits do not segregate in accordance with [[Mendelian inheritance#Mendel's laws of inheritance|Mendel's laws]].

non-paternity event (also known as misattributed paternity, not parent expected, or NPE) occurs when an individual's presumed father is not in fact their [biological father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_father).

Non-random segregation of chromosomes is a deviation from the usual distribution of [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome)s during [meiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiosis), that is, during [segregation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segregation_(genetics)) of the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) among [gamete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamete)s.

Nondisjunction is the failure of [homologous chromosomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homologous_chromosomes) or [sister chromatids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_chromatids) to separate properly during [cell division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_division) ([mitosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitosis)/[meiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiosis)).

Noninvasive genotyping is a modern technique for obtaining DNA for genotyping that is characterized by the indirect sampling of specimen, not requiring harm to, handling of, or even the presence of the organism of interest.

nonsense mutation is a [point mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_mutation) in a [sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) that results in a nonsense codon, or a premature [stop codon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_codon) in the [transcribed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(genetics)) [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA), and leads to a truncated, incomplete, and possibly nonfunctional [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) product.
Norfolk four-course system is a method of agriculture that involves [crop rotation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crop_rotation).

Normalized chromosome value (NCV) is a mathematical calculation for comparing each [chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) under tested in [cell free DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell-free_fetal_DNA) (cfDNA) for detecting genetic disorder of the fetus.

Norrie disease is a rare X-linked recessive [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) that primarily affects the [eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye) and almost always leads to [blindness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blindness).

Notch homolog 2 N-terminal-like is a family of [proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteins) that in humans consists of 3 proteins (NOTCH2NLA, NOTCH2NLB, and NOTCH2NLC) and is encoded by NOTCH2NL [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

NADPH oxidase, EF-hand calcium binding domain 5, also known as NOX5, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) which in humans is encoded by the NOX5 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
NADPH oxidase activator 1 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the NOXA1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
NADP-dependent oxidoreductase domain-containing protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NOXRED1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Niemann-Pick disease, type C1 (NPC1) is a membrane [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that mediates intracellular cholesterol trafficking in [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.
Neural proliferation differentiation and control protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NPDC1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

npj Genomic Medicine is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that publishes papers on various aspects of genomics and its application in medicine.
Nuclear protein localization protein 4 homolog is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NPLOC4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nucleophosmin (NPM), also known as nucleolar phosphoprotein B23 or numatrin, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NPM1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Neuroplastin is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NPTN [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nuclear DNA (nDNA), or nuclear deoxyribonucleic acid, is the [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) contained within each [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) of a [eukaryotic organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote).

nuclear export signal (NES) is a short [target peptide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_peptide) containing 4 hydrophobic residues in a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that targets it for export from the [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) to the [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) through the [nuclear pore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_pore) complex using [nuclear transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_transport).

Nuclear gene location]] A nuclear gene is a gene whose DNA sequence is located within the [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) of a [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) organism.

definition: nuclear localization sequence, or signal (NLS) is an [amino acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid) [sequence motif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequence_motif) that 'tags' a protein for import into the [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) by [nuclear transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_transport).

nuclear matrix is the network of [fibres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibres) found throughout the inside of a [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) after a specific method of chemical extraction.
Nuclear pore glycoprotein p62 is a protein complex associated with the [nuclear envelope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_envelope).

nuclear receptor 4A3 (NR4A3) (nuclear receptor subfamily 4, group A, member 3) also known as neuron-derived orphan receptor 1 (NOR1) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NR4A3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

nuclear run-on assay is conducted to identify the [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s that are being [transcribed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(genetics)) at a certain time point.
Nuclear sexing is a technique for genetic [sex determination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexing) in those species where XX chromosome pair is present.

Nucleic acids are large [biomolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecule)s that are crucial in all [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) and [viruses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus).

Nucleic acid analogues are compounds which are [structurally analogous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_analog) to naturally occurring [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) and [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA), through substitutions of any of its sugar, phosphate, and nucleobase components.

hybridization (or hybridisation) is a phenomenon in which single-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid ([DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)) or ribonucleic acid ([RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA)) molecules [[Nucleic acid thermodynamics#Annealing|anneal]] to [complementary DNA or RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complementarity_(molecular_biology)).

Nucleic acid methods are the techniques used to study [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s: [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA).

nucleic acid notation currently in use was first formalized by the [International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Union_of_Pure_and_Applied_Chemistry) (IUPAC) in 1970.

Nucleic acid secondary structure is the [basepair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basepair)ing interactions within a single [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) polymer or between two polymers.

Nucleic acid structure refers to the [structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomolecular_structure) of [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s such as [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA).
Nucleic acid tertiary structure is the [[Biomolecular structure#Tertiary structure|three-dimensional shape]] of a [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) polymer.

nucleic acid test (NAT) is a technique used to directly detect a specific [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) sequence, usually to detect and identify a particular species or subspecies of organism, often a [virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus) or [bacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterium) that acts as a [pathogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogen) in [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood), [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)), [urine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urine), etc.

Nucleic acid thermodynamics is the study of how [temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperature) affects the [nucleic acid structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_structure) of double-stranded [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) (dsDNA).
Nucleobindin-1 (NUCB1), also known as calnuc, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NUCB1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nucleofection is an [electroporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroporation)-based [transfection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfection) method which enables transfer of [nucleic acids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acids) such as [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) into [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) by applying a specific voltage and reagents.
Nucleolar and spindle associated protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NUSAP1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nucleolus organizer regions ([American English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_English)) or nucleolus organiser regions ([British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English)) (NORs) are [chromosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) regions crucial for the formation of the [nucleolus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleolus).
Nucleomodulins are a family of bacterial proteins that enter the nucleus of [eukaryotic cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic_Cells).

Nucleomorphs are small, vestigial eukaryotic [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) found between the inner and outer pairs of membranes in certain [plastid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastid)s.
Nucleoporin 188 (Nup188) is a protein that in humans is encoded by the NUP188 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Nuclear pore glycoprotein-210 (gp210) is an essential trafficking regulator in the eukaryotic [nuclear pore complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_pore_complex).

Nucleosides are [glycosylamine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glycosylamine)s that can be thought of as [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide)s without a [phosphate group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphate_group).

nucleoside-modified messenger RNA (modRNA) is a synthetic [messenger RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messenger_RNA) (mRNA) in which some [nucleoside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleoside)s are replaced by other naturally modified nucleosides or by synthetic [nucleoside analogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleoside_analogue)s.
Nucleosome repeat length (NRL) is the average distance between the centers of neighboring [nucleosomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleosomes).
Diphosphoinositol polyphosphate phosphohydrolase 3-beta is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the NUDT11 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Nudix hydrolase 15 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NUDT15 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Bis(5'-nucleosyl)-tetraphosphatase [asymmetrical] is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the NUDT2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nuffield Council on Bioethics is a UK-based independent [charitable body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charitable_organization), which examines and reports on [bioethical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioethical) issues raised by new advances in biological and [medical research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_research).

definition: Nuffield Department of Population Health (NDPH) is an academic department of the [Medical Sciences Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_Sciences_Division,_University_of_Oxford) at the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford).
Nuclear fragile X mental retardation-interacting protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NUFIP1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nullisomic is a [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) condition involving the lack of both the normal [chromosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) pairs for a [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) (2n-2).
Nullomers are short sequences of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) that do not occur in the genome of a species (for example, humans), even though they are theoretically possible.

definition: Nucleoporin p58/p45 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the NUPL1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Nutritional epigenetics is a science that studies the effects of nutrition on gene expression and [chromatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatin) accessibility.

Nutritional genomics, also known as nutrigenomics, is a science studying the relationship between [human genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genome), [human nutrition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_nutrition) and health.

NWD1, short for NACHT and WD repeat domain containing 1, is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) found in [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s, which encodes a protein that contains a [NACHT domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NACHT_domain) and a [WD40 repeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WD40_repeat) domain.

O'Donnell-Luria–Rodan syndrome is an [ultra-rare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra-rare_disease) genetic disorder caused by [pathogenic variant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogenic_variant)s of the [KMT2E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KMT2E) gene.

2'-5' oligoadenylate synthetase-like 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in the [house mouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_mouse) is encoded by the Oasl2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Ornithine decarboxylase antizyme is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the OAZ1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Ornithine decarboxylase antizyme 2 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the OAZ2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

ob/ob or obese mouse is a [mutant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutant) mouse that [eats excessively](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyphagia) due to mutations in the gene responsible for the production of [leptin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leptin) and becomes profoundly [obese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obesity).
Odorant-binding protein 2B is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OBP2B [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
OCC-1 (overexpressed in colon carcinoma-1) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein), which in humans is encoded by the [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) C12orf75.

OCEL1, also called Occludin//ELL Domain Containing 1, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) encoding [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) located at [chromosome 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome_19)p13.11 in the [human genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genome).

Inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase OCRL-1, also known as Lowe oculocerebrorenal syndrome protein, is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) encoded by the OCRL [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) located on the [X chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_chromosome) in humans.
Oculoauricular syndrome is a rare genetic condition affecting the eyes and ears.
Outer dense fiber protein 2, also known as cenexin, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the ODF2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Odonto-tricho-ungual-digital-palmar syndrome is an [autosomal dominant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosomal_dominant) skin condition with salient clinical features of natal teeth, trichodystrophy, prominent interdigital folds, simian-like hands with transverse palmar creases, and ungual digital dystrophy.

Odorant-binding protein 2a is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OBP2A [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
2-oxoglutarate and iron-dependent oxygenase domain containing 1, also known as OGFOD1, is a human [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Ohno's law was proposed by a Japanese-American biologist [Susumu Ohno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susumu_Ohno), saying that the [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) content of the [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)ian [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) has been conserved over species not only in the [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) content but also in the genes themselves.

Okazaki fragments are short sequences of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) [nucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotide)s (approximately 150 to 200 [base pair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base_pair)s long in [eukaryote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote)s) which are synthesized discontinuously and later linked together by the [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) [DNA ligase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_ligase) to create the [lagging strand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagging_strand) during [DNA replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_replication).

definition: Okur-Chung Neurodevelopmental Syndrome (OCNDS) is an [ultra-rare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra-rare_disease) neurodevelopmental syndrome first discovered in 2016.
Olfactomedin 1, also known as noelin 1 or pancortin, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OLFM1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Olfactomedin 4 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OLFM4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Oligogenic inheritance ([Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek) ὀλίγος – ὀligos = few, a little) describes a trait that is influenced by a few genes.
Oligomer Restriction (abbreviated OR) is a procedure to detect an [altered DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_polymorphism) sequence in a [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

Oligonucleotides are short [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) molecules, [oligomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligomer)s, that have a wide range of applications in [genetic testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_testing), [research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recombinant_DNA), and [forensics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forensic_DNA).

Oligonucleotide synthesis is the [chemical synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_synthesis) of relatively short fragments of [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s with defined chemical structure ([sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence)).

Oligotyping is the process of correcting [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequence measured during the process of [DNA sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) based on frequency data of related sequences across related samples.
Oliver–McFarlane syndrome is a condition characterized by [hypertrichosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertrichosis) of the eyebrows and eyelashes.
categories: Genetic disorders with OMIM but no gene

definition: Ollier disease is a rare sporadic nonhereditary skeletal disorder in which typically benign cartilaginous tumors ([enchondroma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enchondroma)s) develop near the growth plate cartilage.
categories: Genetic disorders with OMIM but no gene

definition: Omics is the collective characterization and quantification of entire sets of [biological molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_molecule)s and the investigation of how they translate into the structure, function, and dynamics of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) or group of organisms.
OmniPop is a program used to class populations by [autosomal DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosome) results.

categories: Genetic disorders with OMIM but no gene

definition: Oncogenomics is a sub-field of [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) that characterizes [cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer)-associated [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s.

one gene–one enzyme hypothesis is the idea that [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s act through the production of [enzymes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzymes), with each gene responsible for producing a single enzyme that in turn affects a single step in a [metabolic pathway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolic_pathway).
onion test is a way of assessing the validity of an argument for a functional role for [junk DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junk_DNA).

Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA) is an [online database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_database) of [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes), [inherited disorders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) and [traits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trait_(biology)) in more than 550 animal species.

Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) is a continuously updated catalog of [human genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genome) and [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder)s and [traits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait), with a particular focus on the [gene-phenotype relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype-phenotype_distinction).
Ontario Genomics, formerly the Ontario Genomics Institute, is a not-for-profit organization that manages [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) research projects and platforms.
Oogenesis () or ovogenesis is the differentiation of the [ovum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovum) (egg cell) into a cell competent to further develop when fertilized.
reading frames are defined as spans of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequence between the start and stop [codons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codon).
operational taxonomic unit (OTU) is an operational definition used to classify groups of closely related individuals.

Opitz G/BBB syndrome, also known as Opitz syndrome, G syndrome or BBB syndrome, is a rare [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) that will affect physical structures along the midline of the body.
Green-sensitive opsin is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OPN1MW [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Olfactory receptor family 11 subfamily H member 7 (gene/pseudogene) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OR11H7 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Olfactory receptor 13H1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OR13H1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Orchid Cellmark Ltd is a UK based [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) and forensic testing company with a history of UK and US ownership.
ORFeome refers to the complete set of [open reading frames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_reading_frames) (ORFs) in a [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

Organellar DNA (oDNA) is [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) contained in [organelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle) (such as mitochondria and chloroplasts), outside the [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) of [eukaryotic cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote).

Organic Lake virophage (OLV) is a double-stranded DNA [virophage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virophage) (a virus that requires the presence of another virus to replicate itself and in so doing limits the ability of the other virus to replicate).

origin recognition complex (ORC) is a multi-subunit [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) binding complex (6 subunits) that binds in all [eukaryotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotes) and [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea) in an [ATP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adenosine_triphosphate)-dependent manner to [origins of replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origins_of_replication).
Alpha-1-acid glycoprotein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the ORM1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

orphon is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) located outside the main chromosomal [locus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)), i.e., it may be dispersed to an unconnected genomic location.
Protein OS-9 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OS9 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Oxysterol-binding protein-related protein 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in [humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) is encoded by the OSBPL1A [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Oxysterol binding protein-like 9 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OSBPL9 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
oskar is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) required for the development of the [Drosophila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drosophila) [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo).

Osteomodulin (also called osteoadherin or osteoadherin proteoglycan) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OMD [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Osteonectin (ON) also known as secreted protein acidic and rich in cysteine (SPARC) or basement-membrane protein 40 (BM-40) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the SPARC [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

[Osteoclast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteoclast)-stimulating factor 1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s is encoded by the OSTF1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Ostravik–Lindemann–Solberg syndrome, also known as heart defect-tongue hamartoma-polysyndactyly syndrome, is a rare, multi-systemic [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) which is characterized by [congenital heart defect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congenital_heart_defect)s, [tongue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tongue) [hamartomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamartomas), postaxial [polydactyly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polydactyly) of the hand, and [syndactylism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndactyly) of the foot.

Oto-palato-digital syndrome is the generalised term for two conditions, oto-palato-digital syndrome type I (OPD1) and oto-palato-digital syndrome type II (OPD2), that are both [X-linked recessive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-linked_recessive) genetic disorders with overlapping [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype)s.

Otodental syndrome, also known as otodental dysplasia, is an exceptionally rare disease that is distinguished by a specific phenotype known as globodontia that in rare cases can be associated with eye [coloboma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloboma) and high-frequency hearing loss.
OTU domain containing 6B is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the OTUD6B [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

definition: outron is a [nucleotide sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence) at the 5' end of the [primary transcript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_transcript) of a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) that is removed by a special form of [RNA splicing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_splicing) during [maturation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA_processing) of the final RNA product.
overlap extension polymerase chain reaction (or OE-PCR) is a variant of [PCR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction).

Oxford Centre for Gene Function is a multidisciplinary research institute in the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England).

oxytocin receptor, also known as OXTR, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) which functions as [receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Receptor_(biochemistry)) for the [hormone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hormone) and [neurotransmitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurotransmitter) [oxytocin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxytocin).

P elements are [transposable elements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposable_elements) that were discovered in [Drosophila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drosophila) as the causative agents of genetic traits called [[P element#Hybrid dysgenesis|hybrid dysgenesis]].

P protein, also known as melanocyte-specific transporter protein or pink-eyed dilution protein homolog, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the oculocutaneous albinism II (OCA2) [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
P-type calcium channel is a type of [voltage-dependent calcium channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voltage-dependent_calcium_channel).

P1-derived artificial chromosome, or PAC, is a [DNA construct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_construct) derived from the [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) of [P1 bacteriophages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P1_phage).
Putative P2Y purinoceptor 10 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that, in humans, is encoded by the P2RY10 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
P2Y purinoceptor 11 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the P2RY11 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
P2Y purinoceptor 4 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the P2RY4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

p53, also known as tumor protein p53, TP53, cellular tumor antigen p53 ([UniProt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UniProt) name), or transformation-related protein 53 (TRP53) is a [regulatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regulation_of_gene_expression) [transcription factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_factor) protein that is often [mutated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) in human [cancers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancers).
p53 p63 p73 family is a family of [tumor suppressor gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor_suppressor_gene)s.
p73 is a protein related to the [p53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P53) tumor protein.
Polyadenylate-binding protein 3 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PABPC3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Polyadenylate-binding protein 4 (PABPC4) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PABPC4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Poly(A) binding protein, cytoplasmic 4-like is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PABPC4L [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Pacer (also known as Rubicon-like) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the RUBCNL [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Serine/threonine-protein kinase PAK 6 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the PAK6 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Paleogenomics is a field of science based on the reconstruction and analysis of [genomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomic) information in extinct [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).
Paleopolyploidy is the result of [genome duplications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome_duplications) which occurred at least several million years ago (MYA).
PAN3 poly(A) specific ribonuclease subunit is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PAN3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Pandoraviridae is a proposed family of [[DNA virus#Group I: dsDNA viruses|double-stranded DNA]] viruses that infect [amoeba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amoeba)e.

Pandoravirus dulcis is an egg-shaped virus of genus [Pandoravirus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandoravirus), that was discovered in a shallow lake at [La Trobe University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Trobe_University), Melbourne, [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia) in 2013.

Pandoravirus salinus is a [large virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_Virus) of genus [Pandoravirus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandoravirus), found in the marine sediment layer of the Tunquen River in [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile), and is one of the largest viruses identified, along with [Pandoravirus dulcis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandoravirus_dulcis).

Pangenesis was [Charles Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Darwin)'s hypothetical mechanism for [heredity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity), in which he proposed that each part of the body continually emitted its own type of small organic particles called gemmules that aggregated in the [gonad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonad)s, contributing heritable information to the [gamete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamete)s.
PANO1 is a protein which in humans is encoded by the PANO1 gene.

PANTHER (protein analysis through evolutionary relationships) classification system is a large curated [biological database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_database) of gene/protein families and their functionally related subfamilies that can be used to classify and identify the function of gene products.

Paragroup is a term used in [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) to describe lineages within a [haplogroup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup) that are not defined by any additional [unique markers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unique-event_polymorphism).

parahaplogroup is a term used in [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) to identify a [paraphyletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraphyly) [haplogroup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplogroup).

ParaHox gene cluster is an array of [homeobox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeobox) genes (involved in [morphogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphogenesis), the regulation of patterns of anatomical development) from the [Gsx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gsx_(gene_family)), [Xlox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xlox) ([Pdx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pdx_(gene_family))) and [Cdx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cdx) gene families.
Parallel metaheuristic is a class of techniques that are capable of reducing both the numerical effort and the run time of a [metaheuristic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaheuristic).

paramutation is an interaction between two [allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele)s at a single [locus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)), whereby one allele induces a heritable change in the other allele.

parasexual cycle, a process restricted to [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) and [single-celled organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horizontal_gene_transfer), is a nonsexual mechanism of parasexuality for transferring genetic material without [meiosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiosis) or the development of sexual structures.

Personal genomics or consumer genetics is the [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch) of [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) concerned with the [sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequencing), [analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioinformatics) and interpretation of the [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genome) of an individual.

Personalized genomics is the [human genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_genetics)-derived study of analyzing and interpreting individualized genetic information by genome sequencing to identify [genetic variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation)s compared to the [library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_(biology)) of known sequences.

Personalized onco-genomics (POG) is the field of [oncology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oncology) and [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) that is focused on using [whole genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whole_genome_sequencing) analysis to make [personalized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personalized_medicine) clinical treatment decisions.

Perturb-seq (also known as CRISP-seq and CROP-seq) refers to a high-throughput method of performing [[Single cell sequencing#scRNA-Seq|single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq)]] on pooled genetic perturbation screens.

phene is an individual genetically determined characteristic or [trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trait_(biology)) which can be possessed by an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism), such as eye colour, height, behavior, tooth shape or any other observable characteristic.

phenocopy is a variation in [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) (generally referring to a single [trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trait_(biological))) which is caused by environmental conditions (often, but not necessarily, during the organism's [development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_biology)), such that the organism's phenotype matches a phenotype which is determined by [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) factors.

[phenome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenome)-wide association study, abbreviated PheWAS, is a study design in which the association between [single-nucleotide polymorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-nucleotide_polymorphism)s or other types of DNA variants is tested across a large number of different [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype)s.
phenotype () is the set of observable characteristics or [traits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait) of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism).
Phenotype modification is the process of experimentally altering an organism's [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) to investigate the impact of phenotype on the fitness.

Phenotypic heterogeneity describes different mutations in the same [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) that can sometimes give rise to strikingly different [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype)s.
Phenotypic integration is a metric for measuring the correlation of multiple functionally-related traits to each other.
Phenotypic plasticity refers to some of the changes in an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)'s behavior, morphology and physiology in response to a unique environment.

PiggyBac Transposable Element Derived 5 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the PGBD5 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Pigment dispersing factor (pdf) is a gene that encodes the protein PDF, which is part of a large family of [neuropeptide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuropeptide)s.
Phosphatidylinositol glycan anchor biosynthesis, class N is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PIGN [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Pirbright Institute (formerly the Institute for Animal Health) is a [research institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_institute) in [Surrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrey), England, dedicated to the study of [infectious disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infectious_disease)s of [farm animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livestock).

Pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide, also known as PACAP, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the ADCYAP1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Piwi like RNA-mediated gene silencing 4 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PIWIL4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
PBX/Knotted 1 Homeobox 1 (PKNOX1) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PKNOX1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Plakophilin-2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PKP2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Plant breeders' rights (PBR), also known as plant variety rights (PVR), are rights granted in certain places to the [breeder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_breeding) of a new [variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_variety_(law)) of plant that give the breeder [exclusive control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_right) over the propagating material (including [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed), cuttings, divisions, tissue culture) and harvested material ([cut flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cut_flowers), fruit, foliage) of a new variety for a number of years.

Plant DNA C-values Database (https://cvalues.science.kew.org/) is a comprehensive catalogue of [C-value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-value) ([nuclear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) content, or in [diploid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploid)s, [genome size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome_size)) data for [land plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryophyte) and [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae).
Plant Genetic Systems (PGS), since 2002 part of [Bayer CropScience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayer_CropScience), is a biotech company located in Ghent, Belgium.

definition: Plant genetics is the study of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s, [genetic variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variation), and [heredity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heredity) in [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

Plant transformation vectors are [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid)s that have been specifically designed to facilitate the generation of [transgenic plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgenic_plants).

plantibody is an [antibody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibody) produced by plants that have been [genetically engineered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_Engineering) with animal DNA encoding a specific human antibody known to [neutralize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutralizing_antibody) a particular pathogen or toxin.

Plant–fungus horizontal gene transfer is the movement of [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_material) between individuals in the [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) and [fungus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [kingdoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_(biology)).
Plasmagene is a term used to describe genetic elements that exist outside of the nucleus, typically within the [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) of a cell.

plasmid is a small, [extrachromosomal DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extrachromosomal_DNA) molecule within a cell that is physically separated from [chromosomal DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDNA) and can replicate independently.

plasmid partition system is a mechanism that ensures the stable inheritance of [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid)s during bacterial [cell division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_division).
plasmid preparation is a method of [DNA extraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_extraction) and purification for [plasmid DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid).
plasmidome refers to the [plasmid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasmid)s present in it.

1-Phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate phosphodiesterase beta-2 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the PLCB2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Phospholipase D family, member 5 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PLD5 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Pleiotropy () is a condition in which a single [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) or genetic variant influences multiple [phenotypic trait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait)s.

Pleckstrin homology domain containing, family G member 2 (PLEKHG2) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PLEKHG2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Pleckstrin homology domain-containing family M member 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PLEKHM2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Pleolipoviridae is a family of [DNA virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_virus)es that infect halophilic [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea).
PLINK is a free, open-source [whole-genome association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whole_genome_association_study) analysis toolkit used to perform a wide-range of genetic data analysis.

PLOS Genetics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific) journal established in 2005 and published by the [Public Library of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Library_of_Science).

PLOS Pathogens is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [open-access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-access) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal).
Proteolipid protein 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PLP2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Plexin-A3 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PLXNA3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Plexin-B3 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the PLXNB3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

PncA is a bacterial gene encoding a [nicotinamidase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicotinamidase) that doubles as a pyrazinamidase in [Mycobacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycobacterium) species.

point mutation is a [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) where a single nucleotide base is changed, inserted or deleted from a [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA) sequence of an organism's genome.

Poison exons (PEs); also called [premature termination codon (PTC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_codon) exons or [nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonsense-mediated_decay) exons] are a class of [[Alternative splicing#Modes|cassette exons]] that contain PTCs.

Poisoning the well (or attempting to poison the well) is a type of [informal fallacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Informal_fallacy) where adverse information about a target is preemptively presented to an [audience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audience), with the intention of discrediting or ridiculing something that the target person is about to say.

Pollen [DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_barcoding) is the process of identifying [pollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen) donor [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) species through the [amplification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) and [sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) of specific, conserved regions of plant [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA).
Polony is a contraction of It was finally brought to market by Solexa.

Polony sequencing is an inexpensive but highly accurate [multiplex sequencing technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplex_sequencing_technique) that can be used to “read” millions of immobilized DNA sequences in parallel.
DNA-directed RNA polymerases I and III subunit RPAC2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the POLR1D [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
DNA-directed RNA polymerase I subunit RPA49 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the POLR1E [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) is a family of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s involved in a number of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))ular processes such as [DNA repair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_repair), genomic stability, and [programmed cell death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programmed_cell_death).

Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase family member 14 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that, in [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s, is encoded by the PARP14 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Polycomb-group proteins (PcG proteins) are a [family of protein complexes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein_family) first discovered in fruit flies that can remodel [chromatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatin) such that [epigenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenetic) silencing of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s takes place.

definition: Polydeoxyribonucleotide (PDRN), is a mixture of single-stranded [oligonucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligonucleotide)s with weight ranging from approximately 50 kDa to 1500 kDa, peaking around 350kDa in some commercial forms.

polygene is a member of a group of non-[epistatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistasis) [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)s that interact additively to influence a [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) trait, thus contributing to multiple-gene inheritance (polygenic inheritance, multigenic inheritance, quantitative inheritance Another interest of statistical geneticists using QTL mapping is to determine the complexity of the genetic architecture underlying a phenotypic trait.

Polygenic adaptation describes a process in which a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) adapts through small changes in [allele frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele_frequency) at hundreds or thousands of [loci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(genetics)).
polygenic score (PGS) is a number that summarizes the estimated effect of many genetic variants on an individual's [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype).

PCR inhibitors are any factor which prevent the amplification of [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid)s through the [polymerase chain reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) (PCR).

Polymerase cycling assembly (or PCA, also known as Assembly PCR) is a method for the assembly of large [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) [oligonucleotide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligonucleotide)s from shorter fragments.

Polymerase stuttering is the process by which a [polymerase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase) [transcribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transcription_(genetics))s a nucleotide several times without progressing further on the [mRNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRNA) chain.

pomato (a [portmanteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portmanteau) of [potato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potato) and [tomato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomato)), also known as a tomtato, is a [hybrid plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_plant) that is able to grow both tomatoes and potatoes.

Ribonuclease P protein subunit p29 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the POP4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

population bottleneck or genetic bottleneck is a sharp reduction in the size of a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)) due to environmental events such as [famines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famines), [earthquakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquakes), [floods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floods), fires, [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease), and [drought](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought)s; or human activities such as [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocide), [speciocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinction), widespread violence or intentional [culling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culling).

Population genetics is a subfield of [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) that deals with genetic differences within and among [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology))s, and is a part of [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology).
Population Genetics Group (or PopGroup, or PGG) is an annual meeting of [population geneticists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) held in the UK since 1968.
categories: Population genetics in the United Kingdom

definition: Population genomics is the large-scale comparison of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) sequences of populations.
Population Investigation Committee is a United Kingdom social research group founded in 1936 by the council of the [British Eugenics Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Eugenics_Society).

population size (usually denoted N) is a [countable quantity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Countable_quantity) representing the number of individual [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s in a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology)).

Population structure (also called genetic structure and population stratification) is the presence of a systematic difference in [allele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele) [frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele_frequency) between [subpopulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_(biology))s.

population-based incremental learning (PBIL) is an [optimization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimization_(mathematics)) [algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm), and an [estimation of distribution algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estimation_of_distribution_algorithm).

Portogloboviridae is a [family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_(taxonomy)) of [dsDNA viruses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DsDNA_viruses) that infect [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea).
Portosystemic shunts are a type of [vascular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel) abnormality that causes blood to be emptied into the circulation, without passing through the liver.

Position-effect variegation (PEV) is a [variegation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variegation_(histology)) caused by the silencing of a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) in some cells through its abnormal juxtaposition with [heterochromatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterochromatin) via rearrangement or [transposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposable_element).

Positional sequencing is a method of [sequencing DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) that simultaneously generates information about both identity and location of [nucleotide sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid_sequence).
postgenomic era (or post-genomic era) refers to the time period from after the completion of the [Human Genome Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Genome_Project) (HGP) to the present day.

postzygotic mutation (or post-zygotic mutation) is a change in an organism's [genome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome) that is acquired during its lifespan, instead of being inherited from its parent(s) through [fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertilisation) of two [haploid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haploid) [gamete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamete)s.

Selection coefficient, usually denoted by the letter s, is a measure used in [population genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) to quantify the relative [fitness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_(biology)) of a [genotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype) compared to other genotypes.

selective placement refers to the practice by which [adoption agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoption_agencies) tend to deliberately match certain characteristics of an adopted child's adopted parents with those of that can lead to resemblance between adopted and biological families, for instance, shared social backgrounds and pre-adoption experiences.

Semiconservative replication is the process by which DNA is replicated in all living cells.

sense of a [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) molecule, particularly of a strand of [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) or [RNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNA), refers to the nature of the roles of the strand and its [complement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complementarity_(molecular_biology)) in specifying a sequence of [amino acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid)s.

Syntelog: a special case of [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) [homology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology)) where sets of genes are derived from the same [ancestral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_descent) genomic region.
Synthesis-dependent strand [[Annealing (biology)#Annealing|annealing]] (SDSA) is a major mechanism of homology-directed repair of DNA [[DNA repair#Double-strand breaks|double-strand breaks]] (DSBs).

Synthetic biology (SynBio) is a multidisciplinary [scientific field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_field) that applies the principles of [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering) to develop new biological parts, devices, and systems or to redesign existing systems found in nature.

definition: Synthetic genetic array analysis (SGA) is a [high-throughput](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-throughput_screening) technique for exploring [synthetic lethal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_lethality) and synthetic sick [genetic interactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_interactions) ([SSL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_lethality)).

Synthetic genomics is a nascent field of [synthetic biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_biology) that uses aspects of [genetic modification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_modification) on pre-existing life forms, or [artificial gene synthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_gene_synthesis) to create new DNA or entire lifeforms.
Synthetic lethality is defined as a type of genetic interaction where the combination of two genetic events results in cell death or death of an organism.

Warfarin resistance is a rare condition in which people have varying degrees of tolerance to the anticoagulant drug [warfarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warfarin).
Wiskott–Aldrich syndrome protein family member 3 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WASF3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Watterson estimator is a method for describing the [genetic diversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_diversity) in a population.
WW domain-binding protein 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WBP2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
WW domain-binding protein 4 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WBP4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

WD repeat-containing protein 3 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WDR3 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

tRNA (guanine-N(7)-)-methyltransferase subunit WDR4 is an [enzyme subunit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme_subunit) that in humans is encoded by the WDR4 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
WD repeat domain 47 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WDR47 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
WD repeat-containing protein 5 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WDR5 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

WD repeat containing protein 53 (WDR53) is a protein encoded by the WDR53 gene that has been identified in the human genome by the [Human Genome Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Genome_Project) but has, at the moment, lacked experimental procedures to understand the function.
WD repeat-containing protein 62 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WDR62 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
WD repeat domain 83 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WDR83 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
WDR88 (WD repeat containing protein 88) is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein), which in humans, is encoded by the gene WDR88.

Weismann barrier, proposed by [August Weismann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_Weismann), is the strict distinction between the It is noteworthy in this context that, generally speaking, adult, reproducing plants tend to produce many more offspring in number than animal organisms.

Wellcome Sanger Institute, previously known as The Sanger Centre and Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute, is a [non-profit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-profit_organisation) British [genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics) and [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) research institute, primarily funded by the [Wellcome Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellcome_Trust).

definition: Wernberg coloring, or Wernberg transformation is a way of color-coding [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) [nucleotides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleotides).

Werner syndrome ATP-dependent helicase, also known as DNA helicase, RecQ-like type 3, is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the WRN [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Westerhof syndrome is a cutaneous condition inherited in an [autosomal dominant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosomal_dominant) fashion, characterized by congenital hypopigmented [macule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macule)s.
categories: Genetic disorders with OMIM but no gene

definition: Western Steppe Herders (WSH), or Western Steppe Pastoralists, is the name given to a distinct ancestral component first identified in individuals from the [Chalcolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalcolithic) steppe around the start of the [5th millennium BC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5th_millennium_BC), subsequently detected in several genetically similar or directly related ancient populations including the [Khvalynsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khvalynsk_culture), [Repin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repin_culture), [Sredny Stog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sredny_Stog_culture), and [Yamnaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamnaya_culture) cultures, and found in substantial levels in contemporary populations of [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe), [Central Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Asia), [South Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asia), and [West Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Asia).

Weyer's ulnar ray/oligodactyly syndrome is a rare multi-systemic [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) which is characterized by ectrodactyly, [ulnar, radial, or fibular ray deficit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulnar_dysplasia), and heart, single central incisor, splenic, and renal abnormalities.

WAP, follistatin/kazal, immunoglobulin, kunitz and netrin domain containing 2 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the WFIKKN2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Wheat Improvement Strategic Programme (WISP) is a [Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology_and_Biological_Sciences_Research_Council) (BBSRC) funded collaborative programme for wheat improvement, which brings together experts from five UK institutions: [John Innes Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Innes_Centre), [Rothamsted Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rothamsted_Research), the [National Institute for Agricultural Botany (NIAB)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_of_Agricultural_Botany) and the [University of Nottingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham), and the [University of Bristol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Bristol).

categories: Population genetics in the United Kingdom

definition: White–Sutton syndrome (WHSUS) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder that affects different systems of the human body.

[Woodchuck Hepatitis Virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodchuck_hepatitis_virus) (WHV) Posttranscriptional Regulatory Element (WPRE) is a [DNA sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequence) that, when transcribed, creates a [tertiary structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertiary_structure) enhancing [expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_expression).

William Allan Award, given by the [American Society of Human Genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_of_Human_Genetics), was established in 1961 in memory of [William Allan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Allan_(geneticist)) (1881–1943), one of the first American physicians to conduct extensive research in human genetics.

Witteveen–Kolk syndrome, also known as WITKOS and 15q24 microdeletion syndrome, is a rare [neurodevelopmental disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurodevelopmental_disorder) characterized by developmental delay/[intellectual disability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_disability), [facial dysmorphisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dysmorphic_feature), and [short stature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_stature).
Serine/threonine-protein kinase WNK2 is an [enzyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzyme) that in humans is encoded by the WNK2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Wnt signaling pathways are a group of [signal transduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_transduction) pathways which begin with [proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteins) that [pass signals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_signaling) into a cell through [cell surface receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_surface_receptor)s.

WNT4 deficiency is a rare genetic disorder that affects females and it results in the underdevelopment and sometimes absence of the [uterus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterus) and [vagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vagina).
Wolf distribution is the [species distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species_distribution) of the [wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf) (Canis lupus).

definition: woolly mouse refers to a variety of [genetically modified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_engineering) [laboratory mice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laboratory_mice) created in 2024 by [Colossal Biosciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colossal_Biosciences) as part of a proof-of-concept in [de-extinction of the woolly mammoth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_of_the_woolly_mammoth) through genetically modifying its [closest living relative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_elephant).
WWOX-related epileptic encephalopathy, also known as WOREE syndrome, is a rare genetic developmental disorder.

WormBase is an online [biological database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_database) about the biology and genome of the nematode [model organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_organism) [Caenorhabditis elegans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caenorhabditis_elegans) and contains information about other related nematodes.

definition: RhoU (or Wrch1 or Chp2) is a small (~21 kDa) signaling [G protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G_protein) (more specifically a [GTPase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GTPase)), and is a member of the [Rho family of GTPases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rho_family_of_GTPases).
WS2C is a putative gene associated with [Waardenburg syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waardenburg_syndrome) type 2.

Wu syndrome, also known as X-linked Wu-type intellectual disability, is a rare genetic disorder caused by [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation)s in the [GRIA3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GRIA3) gene located on chromosome Xq25.

X hyperactivation refers to the process in [Drosophila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drosophila) by which genes on the X chromosome in male flies become twice as active as genes on the X chromosome in female flies.
X-linked recessive hypoparathyroidism is a rare, congenital form of [hypoparathyroidism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypoparathyroidism).

X-linked recessive inheritance is a mode of [inheritance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendelian_inheritance) in which a [mutation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutation) in a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) on the [X chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_chromosome) causes the [phenotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) to be always expressed in males (who are necessarily [hemizygous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemizygous) for the gene mutation because they have one X and one [Y chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y_chromosome)) and in females who are homozygous for the gene mutation (see [zygosity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygosity)).

definition: X:A ratio is the ratio between the number of [X chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_chromosome)s and the number of sets of [autosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosome)s in an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism).
Pre-mRNA-splicing factor SYF1 is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that in humans is encoded by the XAB2 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
Xanthine dehydrogenase, also known as XDH, is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) that, in humans, is encoded by the XDH [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Xenopus egg extract is a lysate that is prepared by crushing the eggs of the [African clawed frog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_clawed_frog) [Xenopus laevis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenopus_laevis).

XK Related 7 (XKR7) is a protein predicted to be a [transmembrane protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmembrane_protein) in [Homo sapiens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) encoded by the XKR7 gene.

XMEN disease is a rare [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder) of the [immune system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_system) that illustrates the role of glycosylation in the function of the immune system.

XO sex-determination system (sometimes referred to as X0 sex-determination system) is a system that some species of insects, arachnids, and mammals (not including humans) use to determine the sex of offspring.
